title: SpaceX Targets 13GW of AI Compute Capacity for Colossus 2 by 2027

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The artificial intelligence cloud infrastructure operated by SpaceX is scaling toward an unprecedented level of power capacity, a push that some industry analysts say would be the largest data center buildout by a single company in such a short timeframe. The company has set a target of 13 gigawatts (GW) of compute capacity for its Colossus 2 facility by 2027, which a report from SemiAnalysis compares to the total volume of data center capacity Google established over 27 years from 1999 to 2026.

The growth effort in Memphis is focused on adding nearly 1.2 million Nvidia Blackwell GPUs to the site by the end of 2026. Elon Musk aims to bring roughly 3GW of compute online by December, an increase from the 1.7GW recorded in September. This ramp includes the addition of the "Gun Range" and "Spam" clusters, the latter of which is a repurposed former Hormel products plant configured for AI inference.

selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
Elon’s latest GPU schedule here implies ~2.7 GW of server power (~3+ GW facility) by year-end if the December tranche arrives on time & online vs. his comments on SpaceX’s August expectation of “over 2 GW" back in August.

The math, using its filing’s initial cluster figures:
>GB200: 210 MW ÷ 110k GPUs = 1.91 kW/GPU
>GB300: 220 MW ÷ 110k GPUs = 2.00 kW/GPU
>December: 110k GB200 × 1.91 kW + 1.10M GB300 × 2.00 kW + ~300 MW estimated for Colossus 1 = ~2.7 GW

That puts combined server power at ~1.4 GW now, ~1.8 GW next week and ~2.3 GW in November. +Epoch’s 14% allowance for other IT equipment takes December to ~3.1 GW IT, before cooling and facility losses.

This schedule suggests upside to the earlier outlooks.

selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
SpaceX guided "over 2 gigawatts" of compute by year end.

That was 4 August. 88 days ago.

Tonight Elon says around 1.2M Blackwells at Colossus 2 by year end. That's ~3 GW.

50% more compute than guided. And the stock closed Friday at $134.72, under its $135 IPO price lol

Here's everything you need to know.

1. The ramp

Dec 2025: 0.8 GW
Mar 2026: 1.0 GW
Jun 2026: 1.4 GW
Sep 2026: 1.7 GW
Dec 2026: ~3 GW

Jan to Sep added 0.9 GW. Q4 alone adds ~1.3 GW.

One quarter beats the three before it combined.

2. How the guide moved

4 Aug, Q2 call, Elon: "We expect to end this year with over 2 gigawatts of compute."

20 Oct, Q3 call, Elon: "the roughly 3 gigawatts, maybe 2.5 to 3 gigawatts that we'll have online by the end of this year"

31 Oct, Elon on X: "around 1.2M Blackwells at Colossus 2 by end of year"

2027 got raised too. August: "closer to 10 gigawatts of compute than 5 gigawatts of compute". October: he'd be surprised by anything under 13.

Guide, beat, raise, repeat lol

3. The names

Colossus 2's buildings are now called Macroharder, Minihard, Gun Range and Spam.

Somewhere in Redmond, Microsoft is reading "Macroharder" and not laughing lol

Minihard has 220k GB300s. Nothing mini about it.

Gun Range opens end of November. Fitting, SpaceX keeps shooting past its own guidance.

Spam used to house Hormel products. In December it holds ~200k GB300s for inference. That's ~0.4 GW, or ~$20B a year at $50 a watt. Most valuable can of Spam ever made.

4. What ~3 GW is worth

CFO Bret Johnsen on the Q3 call: pricing is tracking "slightly above the high end of the $30 to $50 per watt range".

$50 a watt a year = $50B a year for every GW.

Elon said in August maybe 10% of compute goes to Grok training. So rent out the other 90%:

3 GW x 90% x $50 = $135B a year from compute

Add Starlink and launch at their Q3 pace, $7.0B a quarter: +$28B

~$163B of run rate going into 2027.

Now line it up:

$58B: Q3 revenue x 4
$100B: the December ARR goal everyone called crazy
$132-148B: the Q1 2027 guide ($33-37B) x 4
~$163B: what ~3 GW can earn

The "crazy" $100B is now the floor.

And the Q1 guide only needs ~2.1-2.4 GW rented at $50 a watt. They'll have ~3. My read: that guide is sandbagged.

5. Why this is so bullish

Payback. Bret: new compute is "generating a payback of less than a year". Every GW that lands early is a year of revenue nobody modeled.

Price. Elon in August: memory supply grows "around 20% per year", demand "by 200% a year, maybe higher". His words: "Economics 101 would suggest that the price increases; it does not decrease." My read: $50 a watt is the floor, not the ceiling.

Scale. ~3 GW is the launch pad. 13 GW at $50 a watt is $650B a year. Elon's own range for end of 2027: $500B to $1T of ARR.

6. Receipts

The night of the Q3 call I posted "$125-$150 B ARR from compute alone by the end of 2026".

Tonight's 1.2M Blackwells puts it at $135-150B.

Bears said 2 GW was a stretch. Said $100B ARR was crazy. Said Elon always misses deadlines.

He's ending the year 50% above the guide.

$1.83T company. ~$163B run rate. That's ~11x.

You are still very insanely early lol

$SPCX
